promises.text: 2024 campaign: Described himself as "a no-nonsense, rugged individualist with a passion for preserving traditional values and local autonomy"; backs protecting personal liberties, budget discipline and smaller government, guided by a "pragmatic resident-first approach".
2024 campaign: "My main campaign promises were transparency, accountability, putting the residents first, and that's what DOGE is all about" (his own later description of his 2024 campaign promises).

electionHistory.text: 2024 universal primary (all voters), County Commission District 1: Won with 50.3% (15,114 votes). Others: Beth Kirshy Narverud (incumbent) 49.7%. Decided in the primary; no District 1 contest on the Nov 5, 2024 ballot.

keyPositions.text: Nov 19, 2024: Sheriff's Office cyber security funds (Item P-6). Voted no. Return of excess FY 2023-24 cyber security funds and request for FY 2024-25 funds passed 3-2; Amsler and Champion voted no.

Feb 25, 2025: County efficiency committee (local DOGE). Proposed. Presented an ordinance for a Hernando County Department of Government Efficiency. Said: "I'd love to see some bidding on some of our jobs so that we're driving some of the free market there." No vote was reported.

Jan 24, 2026: Flock license plate reader cameras. Proposed an ordinance; objected to installation without board approval. Said: "Government works best when it works in the light." No vote; the board agreed to hold a workshop.
May 8, 2026: Half-cent sales tax referendum for roads. Voted yes (motion failed 3-2). Only Champion and Amsler voted to put the roads surtax on the November ballot.

2020 primary, County Commission District 3: Won with 68.7% (25,515 votes). Others: Burton Melaugh (REP) 31.3%. No District 3 contest on the Nov 3, 2020 general results page.
2024 Republican primary, County Commission District 3: Won with 61.3% (11,660 votes). Others: Marvin Baynham (REP) 38.7%

keyPositions.text: Jan 30, 2019: Firing County Administrator Leonard Sossamon. Voted yes (passed 3-2).

Mar 7, 2023: Impact fee increases (workshop). Supported reviewing fee categories; disagreed that impact fees would hurt growth. On drive-through car washes: "I don't think we're categorizing (drive-through car washes) properly".
Mar 28, 2023: Surplus county property sales (Casey Road, Eagle Drive, Oakhurst Drive). Voted yes (adopted 3-2). Aye: Allocco, Campbell, Hawkins. Nay: Narverud, Champion.

Study of raising school impact fees all at once. Supported (implied by 3-2 count). Said the county is not prepared for the influx of school students and adults seeking homes and recreation (reporter's paraphrase). The article names only Champion and Campbell as no votes.
Nov 19, 2024: Sheriff's Office cyber security funds (Item P-6). Voted yes (passed 3-2).
Mar 3, 2026: Seville West master plan revision. Questioned late-filed documents. Said: "The public is wondering what's going on." The plan passed 3-2; the article does not give individual votes.

May 8, 2026: Half-cent sales tax referendum for roads. Did not support placing it on the ballot (by implication of the 3-2 vote). Said: "If we do nothing, if we don't shift any ad-valorem millage, we're going to get exactly what we have right now."
Jun 2, 2026: Data center moratorium. Supported. Said he is not opposed to data centers but wants guardrails: "If you're not proactive, you're going to get run over."

votes.inShort: Approved a mediated settlement agreement with Raysor Ventures, LLC dated Jan 10, 2025, with modifications including 90 units, delivering conservation land and a set mix of bedroom sizes.
votes.officialTitle: Mediated Settlement Agreement With Raysor Ventures, LLC, Dated January 10, 2025, and Associated Resolution
votes.motion: To approve the staff recommendation with modifications of 90-units, delivering the conservation land, no fence, 15% at 3-bedrooms, 45% at 2-bedrooms and unlimited for 1-bedroom units, with 10% holiday parking and to work with the County regarding a bus stop/sidewalk. (Resolution No. 2025-039).

does.text: Settles a land use dispute with Raysor Ventures, whose request to rezone agricultural land for multifamily housing the board had denied 5 to 0 in June 2024. The settlement approves the rezoning (file H2427) with added conditions in the motion: a 90-unit limit, delivery of conservation land, no fence, a set bedroom mix and work with the county on a bus stop and sidewalk. Each side pays its own legal fees.

after.text: The board adopted Resolution No. 2025-061 to correct a scrivener's error in the settlement resolution.

votes.headline: Declared county land on Kane Road surplus and donated it for affordable housing
votes.inShort: Declared county-owned property on Kane Road surplus and approved donating it to Mid Florida Community Services (You Thrive Florida) for affordable housing.
votes.officialTitle: Declaration of County Owned Property Located on Kane Road as Surplus Property and Consideration of Donation to Mid Florida Community Services, Inc., d/b/a You Thrive Florida for Affordable Housing (Key #321342)

does.text: Declares a vacant 10,728-square-foot county lot on Kane Road in Spring Hill (valued at $39,666) surplus and gives it to the nonprofit You Thrive Florida to build an owner-occupied affordable home. The deed requires the land to stay affordable housing for 30 years and construction to be finished within 30 months, or the lot goes back to the county. State SHIP housing funds may help pay for construction once a building permit is approved.

does.text: The ordinance would have expanded the area of Hernando County where universal (mandatory) garbage collection applies. Because it failed 1 to 4, the district boundaries set in 2013 stay the same, and a companion resolution was not heard. The board then agreed to have staff prepare an item on a possible 2026 ballot referendum on expanding universal collection.
